summary.suggested: The St. Louis Republic reported that Tom Allen lay seriously ill with persistent colds at his home on Market Street between Sixth and Seventh, and recalled his fights with Joe Goss, Jem Mace, Mike McCool and Charlie Davis.

metadata.notes: Masthead: The Republic: Saturday, January 31, 1903, page 4.

facts.fact: Allen was confined to his bed and believed seriously ill with persistent colds of two or three weeks, at his home on Market Street between Sixth and Seventh
places: Market Street between Sixth and Seventh, St. Louis

facts.fact: Allen knocked out Charlie Davis in five rounds for the championship of England, said to be the first championship fight in England under Queensberry rules; he received a purse of £100 and a silver cup that hung over his bar
Allen fought Joe Goss for the heavyweight championship in 1867; the bout ended in a riot and Allen's seconds were mobbed
Allen fought Jem Mace in Louisiana in 1870 for the heavyweight championship and $5,000; his seconds threw up the sponge after ten rounds (50 minutes) when he injured his arm
Allen beat Mike McCool in seven rounds on Bloody Island near St. Louis

notes: Career facts are a 1903 retrospective and secondhand (medium confidence); it puts his start at age 21 in 1860 and his birth in 1839. Don Murphy is named as manager of Allen's place.
